context: 1. Give TableScrollHint a scroller target (ref or id) so it can measure. 2. Replace the breakpoint gate with measured overflow (scrollWidth > clientWidth) via ResizeObserver plus a post-hydration check. 3. Fold PlatformIndex's span and QueryHeatmap's chip into the component. 4. Add ResizeObserver and scrollWidth/clientWidth geometry shims to src/test/setup.ts, or existing component tests regress for a mechanical reason. 5. Add ONE rule to the existing scan_explorer_tokens.py family: no page-local scroll-hint markup. That is a ban on a known literal pattern, which is all a source scan can honestly enforce.
description:
.bb-scroll-affordance is display:none above 48rem (index.css), so every TableScrollHint consumer only shows a cue on mobile. At 1440px the cross-benchmark matrix cuts mid-value and the Query results table ends at 'POW...' with nothing indicating more columns exist.

Two pages worked around this independently rather than fixing the component: PlatformIndex.tsx:686 hard-codes a plain <span>, and QueryHeatmap.tsx:586-597 ships its own `hidden md:block` chip labelled 'Query columns ->' which reads as a control rather than a scroll cue.

Blocking constraint: TableScrollHint is currently a SIBLING of the overflow-x-auto div (MetaLeaderboard.tsx:259-265), so it has no scroller to measure. The component needs a ref/target API before overflow-driven behaviour is possible.

anti_patterns.dont: add the ResizeObserver change without the JSDOM shim
anti_patterns.instead: land the shim in src/test/setup.ts in the same PR
anti_patterns.why: JSDOM reports 0 for layout metrics, so every consumer test would evaluate to false

anti_patterns.dont: claim a general anti-fork architectural guard
anti_patterns.instead: add one literal-pattern rule to the existing scanner
anti_patterns.why: a source scan cannot recognise semantic reimplementation; all three reviewers rejected the broader claim

anti_patterns.instead: make worktree-create BRANCH=... WORKTREE_PATH=... then make agent-write-preflight
anti_patterns.why: AGENTS.md makes the primary clone read-only for agents

anti_patterns.dont: flip the breakpoint or add a second breakpoint
anti_patterns.instead: measure actual overflow on the scroll container
anti_patterns.why: column counts vary per benchmark; no breakpoint predicts overflow

preserves.behavior: QueryHeatmap's cloned sticky header (QueryHeatmap.tsx:598) keeps working
Sticky first columns already exist: MetaLeaderboard.tsx:273-280 (Platform) and QueryHeatmap.tsx:669-732 (four frozen columns). Do not re-add them.
The 48rem mobile behaviour must remain correct; this widens when the cue appears, it does not remove mobile support
